headline: The last of Thursday's rain band moves through San Diego County this afternoon and showers taper off by Friday morning, leading into a mostly dry, notably cool stretch through early next week, with an uncertain storm possible around the Wednesday before Thanksgiving.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: A weakening cold front is pushing its band of moderate to heavy rain across San Diego County Thursday afternoon, with rain falling at up to about half an inch per hour at times over the metro and coast (including Carlsbad), after rates of 0.40–0.60 inch per hour and totals near 1 inch on the coastal slopes near the LA County line. Scattered showers follow behind the front, tapering off Thursday evening in Orange County and the Inland Empire and lasting until Friday morning in San Diego County, while low clouds slowly break up from west to east. Gusty west winds blow along the desert slopes of the mountains Thursday evening and ease overnight (the mountain and pass Wind Advisory ends at 4 PM). Snow levels drop to near 6,000 feet by late afternoon, and Big Bear Lake could pick up about half an inch of snow.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Friday turns mostly sunny by afternoon, though isolated light showers may linger over parts of the San Diego metro in the morning. It will be cool, with highs 5 to nearly 15 degrees below normal: only 30s and 40s in the mountains and 50s in the high desert. Saturday and Sunday stay cooler than normal with more clouds, as a weak disturbance moves through Northern California while another storm nears the Pacific Northwest.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Part of that weak disturbance may drift south and spin up over the desert Southwest, bringing a slight chance of very light showers or drizzle near the coast Sunday night into Monday morning; anything that falls will be light. Early next week looks dry and cool. Heading toward Thanksgiving, a large storm system over the northeast Pacific could either stay north as high pressure builds in from the south (dry and warmer here) or split, with part of it moving closer to bring potentially wetter weather around Wednesday; forecasters stress it is still about a week out, so check back.

coast: A building northwest swell keeps surf at 3–6 feet with sets to 7 feet on west-facing beaches through early Friday, with strong rip currents and minor coastal flooding during high tides (Beach Hazards Statement for the Orange and San Diego County coasts through Friday morning). King Tides peak next week: tides above 7 feet are possible as early as Saturday, Nov. 21, and morning high tides may top 8 feet next Tuesday through Thursday, bringing widespread moderate impacts. For boaters, hazardous conditions last through Friday morning, with west winds gusting to about 30 mph (25 knots) and steep, choppy 5–8 foot seas Thursday evening slowly easing Friday morning; a Small Craft Advisory runs until 10 AM Friday for waters out to 60 miles from San Mateo Point to the Mexican border, including San Clemente Island. No further marine hazards are expected through Tuesday.
watch_for: Showers lingering in San Diego County until Friday morning.
King Tides: above 7 feet from Saturday and possibly above 8 feet on morning high tides next Tuesday–Thursday.
Whether next week's storm stays north (dry, warmer) or brings wetter weather around Wednesday before Thanksgiving.
confidence: Forecasters are confident in the front clearing out and the dry, cool stretch Friday into early next week, expect any Sunday night–Monday drizzle to be very light, and have low confidence in the midweek system ahead of Thanksgiving.
